capitals.note: The Dayan Khan page has him relocate to the Kherlen River after a failed Ming counterattack 'the next year' (1501). Hexi Corridor page: 'In 1370, the newly-established Ming dynasty seized the eastern section of the Hexi Corridor from the Mongols' (most of the rest in 1372); Jiayu Pass, built 15 km east of Dunhuang, 'left the city under the control of the Northern Yuan dynasty' (so the city stays Mongol: corrected in the review of fx-52, which keeps a 50 km disc round Dunhuang, 33 cells, out of the subtraction in the keyframes of 1455-1519 and the found event; the subtraction as first written took Dunhuang too, since 502 of its 634 Gansu cells lie west of 98.3 E. Qinghai page: 'under the control of early Ming dynasty', 'later gradually lost to the Khoshut Khanate' (no year), and 'From 1640 to 1724, a big part of the area that is now Qinghai was under Khoshut Mongol control'; no sentence puts the Mongol Khanate there in 1468-1546. Cliopatria's own Mongol shape drops the land in 1547 (0 Gansu and at most 1 Qinghai cell), so the subtraction applies to the keyframes of 1455-1546 that carry the 1468-1521 shapes. The Ming side is not corrected here: ming-dynasty ledger/45 still gives the cells to nobody in 1468, which also drops the 634 corridor cells east of the pass that the Hexi Corridor page leaves Ming.

Dayan died in 1543 (or 1517) and 'by 1540 new regional circles of taijis and local tabunangs' were forming; the Uriankhai were 'conquered in 1538 and mostly annexed by the northern Khalkha' (Northern Yuan page). Fix fx-09 (F294): without the Hami (Kumul) circle, which was Kara Del's, a Ming vassal, to 1513 ('Hami was conquered by Mansur Khan, the ruler of Moghulistan in 1513', Kara Del page; the page's ruler list has Khalil 'originally vassal of Northern Yuan dynasty till 1455, later of Ming dynasty'), never the Great Khan's. Confidence 1: Cliopatria hands the Four Oirats shape to this row in 1475; the Northern Yuan page has only 'Manduulun Khan (1475-1478) effectively won over most of the Mongol warlords' and the infobox 'reunification 1483-1510'. The year 1481 follows the four-oirats dossier, which cites the Oirat Confederation page ('From 1480 on, the Eastern Mongols ... pushed the Oirats westward'; not opened here). Fix fx-09 (F288): the Turpan oases are left out (Turpan Khanate page: the khanate 'ruled the northern part of the Tarim Basin from Turpan in the east' from 1487). [Orchestrator 2 Nov 2026, from fix batch fx-51 (Four Oirat page): the Oirats stayed a separate confederation in Western Mongolia and Dzungaria to 1608 (four-oirats now runs to 1608), so this gain is narrowed to the land outside the Oirat west and dated 1480 to mirror four-oirats' 1480 loss.]

region.text: the Three Guards (Doyin Uriankhai, Ujiyed, Fuyu) and the Ming frontier land of north-eastern Inner Mongolia, western Liaoning, western Jilin and northern Hebei that Cliopatria adds in 1516

ledger.note: By 1495: the Three Guards join Dayan Khan's Mongols. 'By 1495, Batumongke won the Three Guards' (Doyin Uriankhai, Ujiyed, Fuyu), which were incorporated into the six tumens. The year is the page's upper bound; Cliopatria draws the Ming Dynasty land of this increment as Mongol only in 1516, and the page does not locate the Guards or the Xuanhua-Datong frontier forts and cavalry it dates from 1513.
1500: Dayan Khan's court moves to the Eight White Yurts in the Ordos. 'After moving to the Eight White Yurts in Ordos in 1500, they launched a massive attack on Ningxia.'

region.text: Ningxia and the Ordos (attacked from 1500), and the Xuanhua and Datong frontier where the Mongols built forts from 1513

ledger.note: 1500: the Mongols attack Ningxia from the Ordos. 'they launched a massive attack on Ningxia', which brought some lands under their control; raids continued through 1507, Mongol invasions of the Ming 'recommenced' in 1513 with forts at Xuanhua and Datong, and Mongols 'numbering up to 175,000 invaded the Ming Empire in 1514 and 1517'. Drawn as the contested Ming frontier; the pages give no treaty.
1501: the court moves to the Kherlen River after a failed Ming counterattack. The page has Dayan Khan relocate 'to the Kherlen River' 'the next year' after 1500.

region.text: 481 cells at 80-91 E, 42-45 N that Cliopatria moves from its Moghulistan row to this one in 1519; without the Turpan oases

ledger.note: 1519: Cliopatria adds a strip of the Tian Shan foothills and Dzungaria (122,000 km2) from Moghulistan in the year Moghulistan splits in two. Confidence 1: no page opened says the Mongols held it (the Moghulistan page, opened for the eastern-chagatai-khanate dossier, is silent on Mongol involvement). Fix fx-09 (F288): 193 of the 481 cells are the Turpan oases (Turpan Khanate page, founded 1487 'based in Turpan'); they are left out. The rest of the strip stays at confidence 1.

region.text: Ningxia and the Ordos (attacked from 1500), and the Xuanhua and Datong frontier where the Mongols built forts from 1513

ledger.note: 1543: Dayan Khan dies after 'kept defeating the Ming in battle right up until his death in 1543' (Northern Yuan page; the Dayan Khan page has 'In 1542, Dayan Khan lost to Ming troops just before his death' and also dates his death to 1517). The end of the Great Khan's frontier war is entered at his death; no treaty is on the pages, and under Altan the Right Wing made peace with the Ming only in 1571.

region.text: the Right Wing pastures (Cliopatria's Tumed 1547 shape, 7,748 cells, 2.0 M km2) that Altan took

ledger.note: 1547: Altan takes the Right Wing and drives the Great Khan east. 'After Bodi Alagh Khan died, Altan forced his successor, Darayisung Küdeng Khan, to flee eastward'; in 1551 Darayisung 'compromised with Altan and gave him the title Gegeen Khan'. The land is Cliopatria's Tumed shape inside the 1546 shape.

region.text: northern and central Mongolia, the Khalkha lands, that Cliopatria draws in 1547 under its mislabelled 'Golden Horde' row (11,102 cells, 2.8 M km2)

ledger.note: 1547: the Great Khan keeps only the east; the Khalkha lands of Mongolia pass to their own princes. Confidence 1: Cliopatria's year; the Northern Yuan page has 'By 1540 new regional circles of taijis and local tabunangs' and the Uriankhai 'mostly annexed by the northern Khalkha' in 1538, and dates no Khalkha independence. The golden-horde dossier marks the 1547 'Golden Horde' shape wrong and assigns it to the Mongol khanates of Mongolia. [orchestrator, 3 Nov 2026: counterpart 'khalkha' (no slug) -> khalkha-khanates, which starts in 1547 (fx-45 R055)]

region.text: the Chakhar pastures of Ligdan Khan in the east

ledger.note: 1632: Hong Taiji defeats the Chakhars. 'In 1632, Hong Taiji of the Jurchens and his Mongol allies defeated the Chahars and captured Ligdan's family'; Ligdan (Ligdan page) avoided battle and 'fled to Kokenuur' with about 100,000 Chakhar, and died in 1634. Earlier: Ligdan attacked the Jurchens' Mongol allies in 1625 and beat the Khorchin at Zhaocheng in 1628 (Northern Yuan page).
February 1635: Ejei Khan surrenders. 'Ejei Khan surrendered to the Qing and gave the seal to Hong Taiji (February 1635), ending the Kublaid descent ruled Northern Yuan.'

February 1635: the Chakhar lands pass to Hong Taiji's Later Jin (the Qing from 1636). The page says Ejei 'surrendered to the Qing'; Hong Taiji was still Later Jin khan until the Qing proclamation of 1636, so Cliopatria's Later Jin row is the counterpart.
February 1635: the Mongol Khanate of the Great Khans ends with Ejei's surrender, 'ending the Kublaid descent ruled Northern Yuan'.

wars.name: Dayan Khan's reunification of the Mongols
wars.outcome: Dayan Khan unified the Eastern Mongols: a 1483 campaign against Ismayil Taishi, the Three Guards won by 1495, and the Three Right Wing Tumens crushed in 1510, when he killed Mandulai, the Ordos elder; the six tumens in a Left and a Right Wing.
wars.note: The infobox of the Northern Yuan page dates the reunification 1483-1510. The pages give no year for the Oirat war and the six-tumen reorganisation. Internal war: the frontier changes are in the ledger.

wars.name: Mongol-Ming border wars under Dayan Khan

zones.text: Ningxia and the Ordos (attacked from 1500), and the Xuanhua and Datong frontier where the Mongols built forts from 1513

wars.outcome: Raids and invasions: pressure on the Ming from 1495, the attack on Ningxia in 1500 from the Ordos, forts at Xuanhua and Datong from 1513, invasions in 1514 and 1517 ('The high point of Mongol power came in 1517'), a defeat by Ming troops in 1542. No treaty; the frontier is entered as contested.
wars.note: Northern Yuan page: Dayan 'kept defeating the Ming in battle right up until his death in 1543'.

wars.name: Altan Khan's rise against the Great Khan
wars.outcome: Altan became leader of the Right Wing after 1542 and in 1547 forced Darayisung Khan to flee east; in 1551 Darayisung gave him the title Gegeen Khan. The Great Khan keeps the Chakhar east.
wars.note: The Altan page: 'After Gün Bilig's death in 1542, Altan became the de facto leader of the whole of the Right Wing.' The Khalkha loss of the same year (ledger) has no war on the pages.

wars.name: Ligdan Khan's war with the Later Jin and the Khorchin

zones.text: the Chakhar pastures of the east

wars.outcome: Ligdan attacked the Khorchin in 1624 and 1625 and beat them at Zhaocheng in 1628, but in 1632 Hong Taiji and his Mongol allies defeated the Chakhars and Ligdan fled to Qinghai, where he died of smallpox in 1634; Ejei surrendered in February 1635.
wars.note: Ming relations: a 1618 treaty against the Manchus, a 40,000-tael subsidy from 1620, raised to 81,000 after the 1627 revolt (Ligdan page). From 1612 to 1624 the Khorchin, Jarud and southern Khalkha allied with the Jurchens; 'most of the Eastern Tümens deserted to Nurhaci in 1622-24'.

certainty.note: Steppe frontiers throughout; the Ming frontier (Ordos, Ningxia, Xuanhua, Datong) is a war zone with no treaty line. The southern edge in Qinghai and Gansu (1455-1546) and the 1519 Tian Shan strip are the softest, unsupported by any page opened.

notes:
Start and relation to the Northern Yuan. The Mongol khanate page is a disambiguation page that lists 'Northern Yuan (1368-1635)'; the Northern Yuan page runs one Borjigin khanate to Ejei's surrender in February 1635. Cliopatria cuts it in three: Northern Yuan 1375-1439, the Four Oirats 1402-1474 and this Mongol Khanate row 1468-1635. Following the four-oirats dossier (which records Esen's 1455 loss to this row) the dossier starts in 1455 with a new keyframe, not in Cliopatria's 1468; the 1455 start is Esen's death, the page's year, and what stood between 1455 and 1481 was 'different warlords' (soft). The orchestrator may merge this dossier with northern-yuan and four-oirats's Mongol part into one state.
Oirat west 1475-1481: Cliopatria gives it to this row in 1475; the four-oirats dossier keeps it to 1480 on the Oirat Confederation page, which I did not open (page budget 5, spent). I follow the four-oirats dossier (keyframes 1475 adjust, 1481 new, gain 1481 at confidence 1).
The 1516 increment is on the Ming Dynasty 1515 shape, not on Mongol land: 'the Three Guards by 1495' is the page's year and my reading of the land. The 1468-1546 shapes reach Qinghai and Gansu (627,000 km2 overlapping the Ming Dynasty 1467 shape; unverified, no page puts them under the Great Khan; Altan's Qinghai conquest is undated on its page); a gap-filler should open 'Kokonor' or 'Ming Great Wall' pages. The Ming dossier (ea-07) should be checked for the same overlap.
1547: Cliopatria splits the old realm into the small Mongol Khanate (Chakhar, 499,000 km2), Tumed (Altan's Right Wing) and a row it calls 'Golden Horde' (the Khalkha lands, already marked wrong in the golden-horde dossier). The Khalkha need a dossier (counterpart 'khalkha', 1547 to 1691 per that dossier); I give the loss at confidence 1. Nominal Great Khan supremacy over the Tumed and Khalkha under Tumen Jasaghtu ('Under Tümen Jasagtu Khan (r. 1558-92), the realm was unified again') and before Ligdan ('the Eastern Mongol tumens had ceased to function as a unified entity' by 1604) is not drawn as vassalage: the pages do not say vassal.
Not on any page opened: Mongol Khanate area (no infobox figure); Ligdan's capital coordinates (Chaghan city near Abaga Khara Mountain); the six-tumen reorganisation year; Karakorum's fate before 1552; the Oirat war date; Tumen Jasaghtu, Darayisung and Bodi Alagh reign years beyond what is quoted (the infobox and text disagree: Dayan 1478/1480-1517/1543; Ligdan 1603/1604-1634; Tumen 1557/1558-92); rulers are therefore not written. Gazetteer names: none beyond Ordos, Ningxia (region), Xuanhua, Datong. Pages: 5 of 5 (Mongol khanate, Northern Yuan, Dayan Khan, Altan Khan of the Tumed, Ligdan Khan).
